claims.text: Trích XV.3 (hai câu) khớp nguyên văn

sources.quote: recognises only material needs, who realises that men must have food for the body, but is oblivious of the necessity of providing food for the mind
the goods of the mind are at least as important as the goods of the body
If all men were well off, if poverty and disease had been reduced to their lowest possible point, there would still remain much to be done to produce a valuable society

claims.text: XV.2: khoa học có ích cho cả người chẳng biết gì về nó qua phát minh; triết học không, giá trị gián tiếp qua tác động lên người học

sources.quote: If the study of philosophy has any value at all for others than students of philosophy, it must be only indirectly, through its effects upon the lives of those who study it.

claims.text: Trích XV.4 khớp nguyên văn; thiên văn học, tâm lý học, Newton 'mathematical principles of natural philosophy'

sources.quote: as soon as definite knowledge concerning any subject becomes possible, this subject ceases to be called philosophy, and becomes a separate science
Newton's great work was called 'the mathematical principles of natural philosophy'

claims.text: XV.5: vũ trụ có mục đích hay nguyên tử gặp nhau tình cờ; thiện ác quan trọng với vũ trụ hay chỉ với con người; XV.6: từ bỏ hy vọng chứng minh niềm tin tôn giáo

sources.quote: Has the universe any unity of plan or purpose, or is it a fortuitous concourse of atoms?
we shall be compelled to renounce the hope of finding philosophical proofs of religious beliefs
The value of philosophy is, in fact, to be sought largely in its very uncertainty. The man who has no tincture of philosophy goes through life imprisoned in the prejudices derived from common sense
it removes the somewhat arrogant dogmatism of those who have never travelled into the region of liberating doubt

claims.text: Dịch XV.7 (nhà tù, 'là gì'/'có thể là gì', giáo điều ngạo mạn) sát nghĩa

sources.quote: it greatly increases our knowledge as to what they may be

claims.text: Ở chương đầu, Russell bắt đầu từ một cái bàn

sources.where: tên chương I; cái bàn xuất hiện ở đầu chương I (Gutenberg: 'CHAPTER I. APPEARANCE AND REALITY')

claims.text: XV.8: đời sống chỉ xoay quanh lợi ích riêng giống một đồn binh bị vây

sources.quote: we remain like a garrison in a beleagured fortress, knowing that the enemy prevents escape and that ultimate surrender is inevitable

claims.text: Trích XV.9 và XV.12 khớp nguyên văn

sources.quote: In contemplation, on the contrary, we start from the not-Self, and through its greatness the boundaries of Self are enlarged

The impartiality which, in contemplation, is the unalloyed desire for truth, is the very same quality of mind which, in action, is justice, and in emotion is that universal love which can be given to all, and not only to those who are judged useful or admirable.

claims.text: Russell đối lập chiêm ngưỡng với 'sự tự khẳng định' (XV.9); 'công dân của vũ trụ' (XV.12)

sources.quote: Self-assertion, in philosophic speculation as elsewhere, views the world as a means to its own ends
it makes us citizens of the universe, not only of one walled city at war with all the rest
